clue.text: Grotesque yet strong-sounding Scott dominie

indicators.note: the hyphenated 'strong-sounding' says the name is heard as the strongman of the Bible

parts.note: Samson, the Old Testament hero, is the byword for great strength

explanation.surface: A description of a comic schoolmaster in a Walter Scott novel, odd-looking yet with a mighty-sounding name.
explanation.walkthrough: Dominie Sampson is the ungainly tutor in Scott's Guy Mannering; 'Grotesque yet' describes him. The name is said like that of Samson, the strongman of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Abel Sampson, known as the Dominie (Scots for schoolmaster), is a character in Guy Mannering.

clue.text: Farquhar's ruse ascribed to dandies?

parts.note: George Farquhar's comedy is The Beaux' ___: a ruse belonging to the beaux, or dandies

explanation.surface: A literary question about a trick in a Restoration-era comedy played by fashionable men.
explanation.walkthrough: George Farquhar's 1707 comedy is The Beaux' Stratagem; beaux are dandies, so the ruse is theirs.
explanation.definitionFit: A cunning plan or trick to outwit someone is a ruse, as the play's title says.

clue.text: Strange Zion man is novelist whose fame is based on one book

definitions.text: novelist whose fame is based on one book

indicators.note: strange signals that the letters of the next two words are put into an unusual new order

explanation.surface: An odd man from Zion turns out to be a one-book novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' rearranges ZION and MAN. Alessandro Manzoni is famous almost entirely for the novel The Betrothed (I Promessi Sposi).
explanation.definitionFit: Alessandro Manzoni's renown rests chiefly on a single novel, The Betrothed.

clue.text: Indicator of significant stage event

parts.note: read as a theatre lamp that picks out the key moment on the stage, not a phase of a process

explanation.surface: Something that marks an important step in a process.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stage' seems to mean a phase; it is the theatre's stage, where a lamp shows the audience where to look.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre lamp throwing a beam onto one performer draws eyes to the key moment.

clue.text: Japanese drama including a patriarch

indicators.note: including says the drama's name holds the letter that follows inside it

parts.note: Noh is classical Japanese masked drama

explanation.surface: A Japanese play that features an Old Testament patriarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Noah, builder of the ark, is one of the Biblical patriarchs.

clue.text: Comfortable seat for chap with Stevenson's prince

parts.note: Robert Louis Stevenson wrote the novel Prince Otto

explanation.surface: A request for a cosy chair for a man accompanied by a royal from a Stevenson novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Prince Otto (1885) is a Stevenson romance; 'with' only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An upholstered seat or footstool without back or arms, named after the Turks.

clue.text: Duo expires horribly in Greek tragedy

indicators.note: horribly says the letters of duo and expires are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Two people die horribly, as happens in a Greek tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horribly' rearranges DUO and EXPIRES into Sophocles' play.
explanation.definitionFit: Sophocles' play about the king of Thebes is the best-known Greek tragedy.

clue.text: Dr Blimber's head boy gives warning at the wheel

explanation.surface: A schoolboy who acts as a careful driver.
explanation.walkthrough: In Dickens's Dombey and Son, Toots is the senior pupil at Dr Blimber's school. A driver sounds the horn to warn others.
explanation.definitionFit: Toots is the eldest pupil at Dr Blimber's academy in Dombey and Son; a motorist honks the horn as a warning.

clue.text: A son of Duncan in Separate Tables?

explanation.surface: A question whether one of King Duncan's sons appears in Rattigan's play.
explanation.walkthrough: In Macbeth, Duncan's sons are Malcolm and Donalbain. Terence Rattigan's Separate Tables has a character called John Malcolm.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Duncan has an heir by this name, and Rattigan gave the same surname to the journalist in Separate Tables.

clue.text: Inquisitive friend, say, of Gulley Jimson ()

explanation.surface: A prying companion of the painter in Joyce Cary's novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Gulley Jimson is the painter hero of Joyce Cary's The Horse's Mouth; his young admirer is called Nosey.
explanation.definitionFit: Prying means much the same as inquisitive; Nosey Barbon is Jimson's devoted follower in The Horse's Mouth.

clue.text: Final movement from Byron (Don Juan) ()

indicators.note: from says the letters are lifted out of the words that follow, across the gap between them

explanation.surface: A reference to the end of Byron's long poem Don Juan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' takes the letters out of ByRON DOn.
explanation.definitionFit: Classical sonatas and concertos often end with a movement in this form, built on a recurring theme.

clue.text: Shaw's tailor was Greek, and closer in a way

indicators.note: in a way says the letters of and closer are arranged differently

explanation.surface: A claim that a tailor in a Shaw play was Greek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a way' rearranges AND CLOSER; 'was Greek' is extra description. In Shaw's Androcles and the Lion, Androcles is a Greek tailor.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of Androcles and the Lion is a Greek tailor who befriends a lion.

clue.text: Fishes for mythical cave-dwellers

explanation.surface: Something that goes fishing for underground creatures from folklore.
explanation.walkthrough: To troll is to fish by drawing a baited line behind a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Trailing a line from a boat is a way of fishing; Scandinavian folklore puts ugly giants in caves.

clue.text: Generic Deighton novel?

parts.note: the genre of Len Deighton's books, such as The Ipcress File, is espionage fiction

explanation.surface: A question about a typical book by Len Deighton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Generic' means belonging to a genre: Len Deighton wrote thrillers about espionage.
explanation.definitionFit: Len Deighton's novels are tales of secret agents and espionage.

clue.text: The White Horseman displayed a new one

definitions.text: The White Horseman displayed a new one

parts.words: The White Horseman displayed a new one
parts.note: The white horseman also rides in Revelation

explanation.surface: A rider on a pale horse revealed a new catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: The White Horseman was the 1941 anthology of the New Apocalyptics, a group of British poets. The white horseman is also the first rider in the Book of Revelation.
explanation.definitionFit: The end of the world foretold in Revelation, where four horsemen ride, gave its name to the New Apocalypse movement.

clue.text: Awkwardly rig example for composer ()

indicators.note: awkwardly says the letters of rig are put together clumsily in a new order

parts.note: e.g. is the abbreviation for 'for example'

explanation.surface: Advice to fit something clumsily, as an illustration of a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awkwardly' turns RIG into GRI.
explanation.definitionFit: Edvard Grieg was a Norwegian composer, known for Peer Gynt.

clue.text: Reportedly after-death experience in Cymbeline

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is as it is spoken, not as it is spelt

parts.note: something occurring after a person has died is posthumous

explanation.surface: A ghostly encounter beyond the grave in one of Shakespeare's plays.
explanation.walkthrough: Posthumus Leonatus, Imogen's husband, is the hero of Cymbeline; his name sounds like the adjective for things after death.
explanation.definitionFit: Posthumus Leonatus is the banished husband of Imogen in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Beckett's halcyon period

explanation.surface: A reference to a playwright's happiest time.
explanation.walkthrough: Happy Days (1961) is a play by Samuel Beckett.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Beckett wrote the play with this title; halcyon times are carefree, joyful ones.

clue.text: Morley Callaghan's Peggy earns nods somehow

indicators.note: somehow says the letters of earns and nods are put together in some other order

explanation.surface: A woman from a Canadian novel gets approving nods in some way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges EARNS NODS. Peggy Sanderson is the heroine of Morley Callaghan's novel The Loved and the Lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Peggy Sanderson is the central figure of Callaghan's Montreal novel The Loved and the Lost.

clue.text: Amis has its owner writing

parts.note: Kingsley Amis's novel The Biographer's ___: the thing owned by someone who writes lives

explanation.surface: A statement that Amis has someone writing.
explanation.walkthrough: Kingsley Amis's last novel is The Biographer's Moustache: the owner of it is a biographer, a writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Amis's title names facial hair belonging to a writer of lives, the novel's journalist hero.

clue.text: Beastly subject for Iris Murdoch

parts.note: Iris Murdoch's 1963 novel is named after a mythical animal

explanation.surface: An unpleasant topic chosen by the novelist Iris Murdoch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beastly' seems to mean nasty; it means 'of a beast': Murdoch's novel The Unicorn.
explanation.definitionFit: Iris Murdoch's novel The Unicorn takes its title from the fabled one-horned animal.

clue.text: His land beautiful and beloved ()

parts.note: the author of Cry, the Beloved Country, about a beautiful land, South Africa

explanation.surface: A tribute to a man's lovely and cherished homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: Alan Paton wrote Cry, the Beloved Country, a novel of South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Alan Paton, the South African author, called his homeland the beloved country.

clue.text: Jack played by Blunden

parts.note: a jack is a young freshwater predator fish, the subject of a well-known Edmund Blunden poem

explanation.surface: A man called Jack acted by someone named Blunden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' seems to be a man's name; a jack is a young pike, and Edmund Blunden wrote the poem The Pike.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Blunden's poem The Pike describes the fish anglers call a jack when young.

clue.text: Badly ruin colt loose on strange island

indicators.note: badly says the letters of ruin and colt are put into a disordered arrangement

explanation.surface: A careless order to spoil a young horse let loose on an odd island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly' rearranges RUIN COLT. Trinculo is the jester wandering free on Prospero's island in The Tempest.
explanation.definitionFit: Trinculo, the jester in The Tempest, roams at large on Prospero's enchanted island.

clue.text: He had the gall to cure his own blindness ()

definitions.text: He had the gall to cure his own blindness

parts.words: He had the gall to cure his own blindness
parts.note: 'gall' means fish gall, not cheek: in the Apocrypha a blind man's sight is restored with it

explanation.surface: A man brazen enough to treat his own failing sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gall' seems to mean nerve; in the Book of Tobit the blind father is healed with the gall of a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: In the apocryphal Book of Tobit, his son Tobias anoints his eyes with fish gall and he sees again.

clue.text: Booker winner whose early work was bliss ()

definitions.text: Booker winner whose early work was bliss

parts.words: Booker winner whose early work was bliss
parts.note: Bliss (1981) was the first novel of an Australian who later won the Booker Prize twice

explanation.surface: A prizewinning author who found early writing a joy.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Carey's first novel was Bliss; he won the Booker with Oscar and Lucinda and True History of the Kelly Gang.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Carey, the Australian novelist, twice won the Booker after debuting with Bliss.

clue.text: Let fancy be left partly to goddess

indicators.note: partly says only a part of the words is used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: An invitation to let the imagination drift towards a goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partly' takes the run fanCY BE LEft.
explanation.definitionFit: Cybele was the Phrygian mother goddess worshipped in Greece and Rome.

clue.text: Governess in grey, respectable attire the-tls co uk/crossword. Entries submitted

indicators.note: in says the name is held inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A governess dressed in grey, sober clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' takes grEY REspectable; Jane Eyre, Charlotte Brontë's heroine, works as a governess at Thornfield.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Eyre takes a post teaching Adèle at Thornfield Hall.

clue.text: Discretion is not the better part of it, according to Lytton Strachey

definitions.text: Discretion is not the better part of it, according to Lytton Strachey

parts.words: Discretion is not the better part of it, according to Lytton Strachey
parts.note: Strachey wrote that discretion is not the better part of the life-writer's art, twisting the proverb about valour

explanation.surface: A twist on the proverb about valour, attributed to Lytton Strachey.
explanation.walkthrough: In the preface to Eminent Victorians, Strachey said discretion is not the better part of this; he wrote lives of famous Victorians.
explanation.definitionFit: Strachey's Eminent Victorians was a frank, debunking book of lives, and he argued candour matters in writing them.

clue.text: "Clear —— of light thrilling over her uplands " (C. Day Lewis)

definitions.text: "Clear —— of light thrilling over her uplands " (C. Day Lewis)

parts.words: "Clear —— of light thrilling over her uplands " (C. Day Lewis)
parts.note: a gap-fill: the missing word in Cecil Day Lewis's line is a musical term for songs

explanation.surface: A line of verse by C. Day Lewis with one word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The blank in the quotation is filled by the operatic word for solo songs.
explanation.definitionFit: Solo songs in opera fit the line, light thrilling like a voice over the hills.

clue.text: Photograph revealed in petty discord

indicators.note: discord means disagreement, so the letters of in petty fall out of their order

explanation.surface: A picture that comes out during a petty quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discord' rearranges IN PETTY; 'revealed' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A tintype is an early photograph printed directly on a thin iron plate.

clue.text: Clime where Dean Burgon found rose-red city The Crossword is now available on the Internet, at

definitions.text: Clime where Dean Burgon found rose-red city

parts.words: Clime where Dean Burgon found rose-red city
parts.note: Burgon's poem Petra ends 'A rose-red city half as old as time' and begins 'It seems no work of man's creative hand... match me such marvel save in ___ clime'

explanation.surface: A question about the region where a Victorian dean placed a pink city.
explanation.walkthrough: John Burgon's prize poem Petra says 'Match me such marvel save in Eastern clime, A rose-red city half as old as time.'
explanation.definitionFit: Burgon's line sets Petra in an oriental land, the Near East.
